question: What is the ratio of the angles subtended by a chord at the centre of a circle to the angle subtended at any point on the circumference of the circle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the standard **degree measure theorem** of circles, the angle subtended by an arc or chord at the **centre** is always twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the **circumference**.

Let the angle subtended at the circumference be θ.

Then, the angle subtended at the centre is 2θ.

Required Ratio = Angle at Centre : Angle at Circumference = 2θ : θ = 2 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ A circle with **centre O**.

⇒ A **chord AB** subtending an angle ∠AOB at the centre **O**.

⇒ The same chord subtends an angle ∠ACB at point **C** on the circumference.

**Theorem Used:**

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the circumference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/065a2d93c669ae2b48f6c0f63f2e98335f0c24d6f81008d7abc12f7638591eca.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the angle subtended at the circumference be ∠ACB = θ

⇒ According to the theorem, the angle subtended at the centre is ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB

⇒ ∠AOB = 2θ

⇒ Required Ratio = ∠AOB : ∠ACB

⇒ Ratio = 2θ : θ

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 1

**Explanation of Incorrect Options:**

⇒ **Option (1) 3 : 1** is incorrect because the central angle is exactly double, not triple, the inscribed angle.

⇒ **Option (2) 1 : 3** is incorrect because the central angle must be larger than the inscribed angle, making a ratio less than 1 impossible.

⇒ **Option (3) 1 : 2** is incorrect because this represents the ratio of the angle at the circumference to the angle at the centre, which is the reverse of the requested order.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semicircle

An angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always a right angle (90°), which is half of the 180° straight angle at the centre.

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same chord or arc at different points on the same segment of the circumference are always equal.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral always sum up to 180° (they are supplementary).</p
